B1 informal to not know something

C: B1 [ C ] a belief or opinion

我覺得住在鄉村的想法很好，但我不肯定是否喜歡這樣一種現實。

她滿腦子好點子。

我不喜歡住在離家這麼遠的地方。

我根本不知道他們去了哪裡。

我很清楚他們為甚麼早早就離開了。

NONE: B2 perfect, or the best possible
完美的，理想的

C: › [ C ] a principle or a way of behaving that is of a very high standard
理想，標準極高的原則（或行為準則）

S: › [ S ] a perfect thing or situation

example: the ideal employer
無可挑剔的老闆

她是這項工作的理想人選。

這是結識朋友的絕好機會。

理想的世界裡沒有人忍飢挨餓。
democratic ideals
民主理想

我們奉行平等原則。
They share the same high ideals.
他們有著同樣高標準的行為準則。

理想的情形應該是在城裡和鄉下都有住處。

NONE: › the belief that your ideals can be achieved, often when this does not seem likely to others
理想主義

唯心主義，唯心論，理念論

她從未喪失過年輕時的理想主義，終生都在為正義事業而奮鬥。

NONE: › someone who believes that very good things can be achieved, often when this does not seem likely to others
理想主義者
› to think of or represent someone or something as better than that person or thing really is
把…理想化

example: Why do people idealize their school days?
人們為甚麼會把他們的學生時代理想化呢？

NONE: B2 used when describing the perfect situation
理想地，完美地

example: Ideally, I'd like to work at home but it's just not practical.
對我來說最理想的是在家工作，可這根本不現實。

她非常適合這份工作。

NONE: › a belief that someone refuses to change their mind about, even though it may be wrong
固定觀念；偏執

example: This point of view has become something of an idée fixe among political commentators.
這一觀點成了政治評論員們的固定觀念。

NONE: B2 exactly the same, or very similar
完全相同的；極為相似的

example: I've got three identical blue suits.
我有三套完全相同的藍色西裝。

這兩個房間幾乎一模一樣。

雙方的利益可能並不完全相同，但的確也有很多重合之處。
The tests are identical to those carried out last year.
這些測試和去年進行的完全相同。

NONE: › one of two babies of the same sex who were born at the same time, developed from the same egg, and look the same
同卵雙胞胎之一
› able to be recognized
能被識別的

example: In her bright yellow coat, she was easily identifiable in the crowd.
她穿著鮮艷的黃色外套，在人群中很容易認出。

NONE: B2 the act of recognizing and naming someone or something
識別，辨認

身份證（明）

大部分屍體都嚴重燒焦，幾乎無法辨認。

保安人員要我們出示身份證明文件才讓我們進去。

NONE: B2 to recognize someone or something and say or prove who or what that person or thing is
認出，識別
B2 to recognize a problem, need, fact, etc. and to show that it exists
確定；發現

example: Even the smallest baby can identify its mother by her voice.
就連年齡最小的嬰兒也能根據聲音分辨出自己的母親。

週三襲擊事件中的槍手已被確認為李‧吉格斯，一個失業的卡車司機。
The police officer identified himself (= gave his name or proved who he was) and asked for our help.
警官表明身份並請求我們幫助。
The research will be used to identify training needs.
該研究將用來確定培訓的需求。
You need to identify your priorities.
你需要確定自己優先要做的事情。

NONE: › to believe that someone or something is closely connected or involved with something
認為…與…密切相關

example: Many football fans are unfairly identified with violent behaviour.
許多足球迷被不公正地與暴力行為相提並論。

NONE: B2 to feel that you are similar to someone in some way and that you can understand that person or their situation because of this
認同（某人），與（某人）產生共鳴

example: Many women of normal weight feel unable to identify with the super-thin models in fashion magazines.
許多體重正常的女性對時尚雜誌中那些超瘦的模特兒無法產生認同感。

NONE: › very similar in appearance, in a way that is boring and has no character
外表千篇一律的

› a picture of the face of someone who the police want to question, usually because that person is thought to have been involved in a crime. The picture is made from a collection of drawings of noses, eyes, ears, etc. and is based on the descriptions of witnesses to the crime
（幫助警方識別罪犯的）艾登蒂基特容貌拼圖（由一套繪有各種類型的鼻子、眼睛、耳朵等的圖畫拼成）

example: He's been seen out at nightclubs and restaurants with a series of identikit blondes.
人們多次看見他在夜總會和餐館與一些長相千篇一律的金髮女郎在一起。
an Identikit picture
用艾登蒂基特容貌拼圖拼成的畫像

警方發放了他們想要訊問的男子的合成模擬頭像。

photofit (picture)

NONE: B2 who a person is, or the qualities of a person or group that make them different from others
身份；本身；特性

在獄中人們經常會失去自我。

NONE: B1 an official document or card with your name, date of birth, photograph, or other information on it that proves who you are

NONE: › a row of people, including a person who is believed to have committed a crime, who are shown to a witness (= person who saw the crime) to find out if the witness recognizes that person

› a written sign or symbol that represents an idea or object, used in some writing systems such as Chinese
（漢字等）表意文字；表意符號
› based on or relating to a particular set of ideas or beliefs
思想體系上的，意識形態上的

NONE: › a person who believes very strongly in particular principles and tries to follow them carefully
